qs.q: An infant presents with macrocephaly and symptoms of increased intracranial pressure. Neuroimaging reveals an intraventricular papillary neoplasm in the lateral ventricles. Which tumor is most likely?
qs.e: Choroid plexus tumors are the most frequent CNS tumor in infants under 1 year of age, occurring predominantly supratentorially in the lateral ventricles. They typically present with signs of increased intracranial pressure and macrocephaly in infants.

qs.q: In an infant whose cranial sutures have not yet fused, increased intracranial pressure most commonly leads to:
qs.e: Open sutures allow the skull to expand, producing a large head (macrocephaly). Adults with closed sutures would instead develop raised ICP without head enlargement.

qs.q: Which pathological entity is classified as a compensatory ventricular enlargement due to a loss of brain parenchyma rather than true increased intracranial pressure?
qs.e: Hydrocephalus ex vacuo occurs due to neurodegeneration or infarcts resulting in loss of brain parenchyma, and it does not raise intracranial pressure. True hydrocephalus involves excessive CSF accumulation that typically elevates intracranial pressure.

ai.summary: ICP is a life‑threatening state where brain pressure rises above 20 mmHg. In low‑resource settings it is often secondary to infections, trauma or hydrocephalus. Rapid recognition and decompression are essential.

sections.p: ICP is the pressure within the skull, normally 5–15 mmHg. In children, a sustained pressure >20 mmHg is considered raised and requires urgent action.

exam: What is the first step in a child with suspected raised ICP? — Assess airway, breathing, circulation; check pupils; obtain fundoscopy; consider urgent CT if available.
How would you differentiate raised ICP from severe dehydration? — Dehydration shows dry mucosa, sunken eyes, no papilloedema; raised ICP shows papilloedema, vomiting, cranial nerve palsy.
Why is dexamethasone used in tuberculous meningitis with raised ICP? — It reduces meningeal inflammation and cerebral oedema, lowering ICP.
What is the danger of giving NSAIDs to a child with raised ICP? — They can impair platelet function and increase bleeding risk, worsening intracranial haemorrhage.
When is a lumbar puncture contraindicated in suspected raised ICP? — Fixed dilated pupil or signs of herniation; risk of herniation during LP.
What is the significance of an opening pressure >250 mmH₂O? — It confirms raised ICP and may necessitate CSF diversion.

How do you manage a child with hydrocephalus and raised ICP in a setting without neurosurgery? — Start acetazolamide, consider external ventricular drain if available, and arrange transfer if possible.
